messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: Plot with slope and 95% CI lattice style
parts:
Dear list members,

I want to reproduce this plot made with lattice in ggplot2 and also to
plot the slope and 95% CI from a linear model. In fact, the plot is
from data that was analyzed using the function lmer (mixed model)
from the package lme4.

xyplot(ipa ~ tiempo | localidad, data=ipa, type = c("p", "g", "r"),
pch=19, col="Black", strip = strip.custom(bg = "grey",
par.strip.text=list(cex =0.5)))

I tried this to start, but is not giving me the same results

p <- ggplot(ipa, aes(tiempo, ipa)) + geom_point()
p + facet_grid(. ~ localidad)


Thank you very much in advance.
Best,

Manuel Spínola

messages.subject: Re: Plot with slope and 95% CI lattice style
parts:
Manuel, 

Much easier that way. 

This is what I came up with. facet_wrap() is probably what you were mainly looking for. facet_grid() would require you to have another factor to divide up the towns, whereas facet_wrap() does the rows by dividing up the plots evenly. stat_smooth() adds your lines. I picked method=lm for basic linear modeling and disabled the standard error shading. I added theme_bw() to make it look more like the xyplot.
p <- ggplot(ipa, aes(tiempo, ipa)) + geom_point()

p +  facet_wrap(~localidad) + stat_smooth(method=lm, se=F)+theme_bw()

There is one issue with it though. It does not like the name COLONIA.PURISCALE\xd1A. I am not entirely sure why, but I'm guessing it has something to do with the "\".

Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plot with slope and 95% CI lattice style
parts:
Hi:

Does this work out for you?

# Copy localidad to a new variable in ipa (localidad2...inspiring, I know :),
# and use gsub to replace the dots by spaces

ipa$localidad2 <- as.character(ipa$localidad)
ipa$localidad2 <- gsub('\\.', ' ', ipa$localidad2)

# Redefine the plot with the modified data frame:
p + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = TRUE) +
      facet_wrap(~ localidad2) +
      opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(size = 6)) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = 1:4)


The opts() line shrinks the text size in the strip panels. I think 6 looks good,
but you can play with the size to get what pleases you, because that's
what counts. The last line is to avoid overlapping of x-axis labels.

HTH,
Dennis

Dennis, 
It mostly worked for me, but the ñ was still throwing a wrench into the works. 

In the end the following gave me the attached graph, which is very very similar to the lattice graph. 

ipa<-read.delim("/Users/brandonhurr/Desktop/ipaloc.txt")

ipa$localidad2 <- as.character(ipa$localidad)
ipa$localidad2 <- gsub('\\.', ' ', ipa$localidad2)

#may be platform specific?
ipa$localidad2 <- gsub('COLONIA PURISCALE\U3e34383cA', 'COLONIA PURISCALEÑA', ipa$localidad2)

ggplot(ipa, aes(tiempo, ipa)) +
geom_point()+

geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = TRUE) +
facet_wrap(~ localidad2) +

scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = 1:4) +
theme_bw()+
opts(strip.text.x = theme_text(size = 6))

#I forgot about gsub()

Brandon
